xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4557: Herdr terminal attach drops bracketed-paste mode, so multi-line paste is sent as separate lines

plan.title: Herdr terminal attach drops bracketed-paste mode, so multi-line paste is sent as separate lines
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: On a Herdr host the browser xterm starts with bracketed paste off. Herdr's first full terminal.frame repaints the grid but never replays DEC private modes (live probe: only ?2026h ?25l ?25h ?2026l), Herdr exposes no mode state anywhere, and XTerminal.tsx calls term.reset() before writing the snapshot. So a multi-line paste goes out as raw text with \r between lines and can reach the agent as separate submitted lines. Separately, the right-click context-menu Paste sends clipboard text straight to the WebSocket, bypassing xterm's bracketing and \n to \r conversion on every backend.
narratives.Proposal: In serveHerdrTerminal (src/dashboard/server/ws-terminal.ts), prefix the first Herdr frame, the one sent as the snapshot control frame, with \x1b[?2004h. This is safe because Herdr's attach input path (apply_terminal_attach_input, herdr v0.9.1 src/server/pane_input.rs) re-wraps a complete bracketed paste to the pane's live mode, so apps that never enabled bracketed paste receive plain text. Route the context-menu paste through term.paste(text). Document the Herdr snapshot mode gap in docs/TERMINAL-BACKENDS.md and docs/DASHBOARD-ARCHITECTURE.md. Full detail, before/after snippets and verified Herdr source references are in .pan/drafts/PAN-4557.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Injecting mouse-reporting (?1000/?1002/?1003/?1006) or focus (?1004) modes, or any DEC mode other than 2004 — it would re-break the drag-select fix in 5d2dafcf16d
- Prefixing later Herdr frames, or changing decodeTerminalRecord / HerdrTerminalProcess.pump
- Changing the tmux attach path (captureFreshSnapshot, captureViewportSnapshot, PTY hub)
- Changing the RPC TerminalService.streamSession path (no frontend xterm consumer)
- Changing Herdr itself; an upstream request for mode state in terminal.frame is a possible follow-up, not this issue
- Sanitizing paste payloads for lone surrogates in controlTerminal.write (PAN-4506 scope)
- Raising any scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt cap
narratives.UAT: Browser UAT for the test role (Herdr host, isolated Playwright profile, throwaway conversation — never a live work agent or a shared browser session): (1) after attaching a Herdr-backed terminal view, xterm term.modes.bracketedPasteMode reads true; (2) pasting "PASTEME line1\nline2" with the keyboard paste gesture sends exactly "\x1b[200~PASTEME line1\rline2\x1b[201~" over /ws/terminal; (3) the agent composer renders one pasted block (both lines, or a [Pasted text placeholder) and does not submit line1 as its own turn.

autoDecisions.summary: Force ?2004h into the Herdr snapshot instead of replaying Herdr's mode state.
autoDecisions.rationale: Herdr v0.9.1-0.9.5 exposes no pane mode state (pane get, process-info, api snapshot, socket-api.mdx, and the observe stream all lack it), so replay is impossible. Herdr's apply_terminal_attach_input normalizes a complete bracketed paste to the pane's live mode, so always-on bracketing in the browser matches Herdr's own client contract and is safe for panes that never enabled it.

autoDecisions.summary: Apply the prefix only to the first frame, inside serveHerdrTerminal.
autoDecisions.rationale: The client resets xterm before writing the snapshot, so the prefix must be inside the snapshot data. Applying it to later full frames would override an app that turned bracketed paste off after attach.

autoDecisions.summary: Also fix the context-menu Paste to use term.paste(text).
autoDecisions.rationale: It shows the same symptom (multi-line paste arrives as separate lines) on both backends. It is a one-line change that also shrinks XTerminal.tsx, which sits at its file-size cap.

autoDecisions.summary: Leave mouse and focus modes unreplayed.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue names only bracketed paste as the observed harm. Forcing mouse modes would break the drag-select fix in 5d2dafcf16d, and Herdr encodes mouse input on its side via terminal.mouse.
